why: Names paired with the reading each must produce. This is the whole statement of the grammar `pages/domain/seat-name.domain.md` declares: three forms a name may take, and which reading wins where more than one set of stated values would spell one. Every case is a name a seat could carry, so a case that stops reading is a name that stopped being addressable.

collisions.why: Every persona slug and every role slug is also a domain slug, because Alan ruled domain the supertype every other kind hangs beneath. That is the whole reason a segment can be read more than one way, so the fixture states it rather than testing a set of slugs where it does not hold.

split-differently.why: The negative control, and it is deliberately tiny. Two readings divide `a-b-c` in different places, so they disagree about a character that is a boundary in one and a slug's own hyphen in the other — and a boundary is comparable only to a boundary, so neither is narrower. A wider vocabulary here would admit further divisions and stop measuring the tie. The split runs between the domain and the role, no persona being spelled beside either.

cases.name: amy
cases.why: A seat whose principal is Alan, spelling its persona's name and nothing else. `amy` is a persona slug and a domain slug both, so two of the three forms spell this name, and the persona is drawn from the narrower vocabulary — which is the whole of what `the narrower reading wins` settles here.

cases.name: manager
cases.why: The same tie with no persona in it, so nothing reads that rule as a rule about personas: a lone segment that is a role slug and a domain slug reads as the role.

cases.name: amy-alan-handler
cases.why: A handler, the one form spelling an identity in front of a domain and a role. Alan's own inbound path carries this name live. The form is keyed on the role rather than on the principal: his principal would otherwise take the short name, and every seat serving somebody else would answer to the same address as the one serving him.

cases.name: alan-handler
cases.why: A handler nobody has been authored over, spelling the person it serves and its role and no identity. It reads through the same form every other seat does, which is what keeps an unauthored inbound path addressable.

cases.name: memory-worker
cases.why: A segment reads as a role rather than as the domain a role also declares.

cases.name: all-about-alan-recorder
cases.why: A hyphenated domain in front of a role, which is where reading left to right would have to guess where the domain stops. `alan` is a domain of its own here too, so the head has a shorter reading available and the whole one is what it takes.

cases.name: agent-harness-manager
cases.why: A domain and a role, with no identity in front of either. Held beside `manager` alone, this is what says the head fills the domain slot rather than being read as the role a segment also declares.

cases.name: alan-harness-lead
cases.why: A seat working for an agent whose persona IS stated and is not spelled: this is the name a seat holding `amy` in `alan-harness` as its lead composes. A name spelling her too would move whenever she moved, and she is not what such a seat is reached by.

cases.name: memory-worker-flex-2
cases.why: A flex value is a shape rather than a vocabulary, so it needs no declaring here. It spells after the attributes, which is what tells two otherwise identical seats apart.

cases.name: agent-harness-developer-build-singleton-deploy
cases.why: The whole shape a seat working for an agent spells: every attribute and assignment it states except its persona. Both the domain and the task carry hyphens of their own.

cases.name: agent-harness-developer-build-singleton-deploy-18014
cases.why: A name no seat can carry: a bare number fills no slot this grammar declares, so a trailing one leaves the whole name reading as nothing. It is held beside the same seat's live name so the two cannot both be addressable.

cases.name: claude-domain-lead
cases.why: The defect measured on 2026-08-06 across the fleet's live names, and now a name no seat can carry at all: a persona is spelled alone, or in front of the person a handler serves, and never in front of a domain and a role. Nine live seats wore this and each spells `domain-lead` now. It reads as nothing rather than as the seat it used to name, which is the answer that leaves the old spelling visible instead of quietly re-pointed.

cases.name: ki-handler
cases.why: A real person's handle in front of a role — the live inbound path for two people. The reading draws every segment from a vocabulary and `ki` is in none, so this reads as nothing at all. It is NOT a name this system refuses: the code repository's looser `seated-persona` family holds it, and this case is what fixes which of the two answers it.

cases.name: nobody-here
cases.why: A name drawn from no vocabulary reads as nothing, which is a different answer from a tie and is reported as one.

cases.name: a-b-c
cases.why: Two readings divide the name in different places, so neither is narrower and the name cannot be addressed. This is the case a rule that ranked every pair would answer on, and answering it is what would stop the fleet ever reporting a name nobody can read.
